Reading and information

Translation and reading in your native language

First translate needed foreign-language material into your native language, then read and understand it in that language, spending attention on content and relationships. For someone whose native and habitual reading language is Chinese, explanations, navigation, comparisons, progress, and results should normally be in Chinese. Other readers can choose according to their own language and habits. Return to the foreign-language original for key terms, disputed arguments, or unclear passages. Understanding a subject need not first become an English test; switch reading modes deliberately when language practice is your purpose.

  • Long webpages: connect an available translation API to Immersive Translate or Read Frog for bilingual reading. Reduce switching while retaining the original for inspection.
  • Selected text, images, and application interfaces: on Mac, Bob supports selection translation, screenshot translation, and translation displayed over the captured image. Select text when possible and capture it when necessary; the recognition and translation services make separate contributions to the result.
  • Longer documents and courses: ask the model to prepare a resumable reading edition, retaining headings, formulas, figures, code, and sources. Translation supports understanding; important definitions and inferences should remain traceable to the original. Localization must not damage formulas or code.

Choose the reading interface and translation API separately

Bob, Immersive Translate, and Read Frog are reading entrances; another service can perform the translation. Translation can begin with free AI. AIHubMix, OpenRouter, and NVIDIA API Catalog offer free models or trial access to examine. Tell the model: “Choose a currently usable free translation endpoint, connect it to my reading tool, and translate a real passage.” Let the model check current activation conditions, model availability, and integration details and carry out the configuration.

Free options are worth trying for occasional words and passages. Whole pages, many consecutive pages, or large document collections generate more requests and are more likely to meet rate limits, waiting, or exhausted allowances. Ask the model to reduce concurrency, retain translations already produced, or compare inexpensive paid endpoints and available subscription capabilities when sustained volume matters. OpenRouter's limits documentation and current provider pages support configuration checks; there is no need to memorize a quota table. The price of the reading interface and the price of its model are separate questions.

Another route connects an existing model subscription through a gateway or reverse proxy you manage, exposing a compatible API to the translation tools. Sub2API is an existing implementation to investigate; local configuration already offers an example connecting this kind of endpoint to Read Frog and Immersive Translate. It uses the upstream subscription's capabilities and limits rather than creating an official API balance. Its project also identifies upstream terms and account risks. Select this route according to the actual account conditions; a working connection does not establish official support.

Let the model align endpoint, authentication key, model name, and protocol. Use a browser extension's OpenAI-compatible settings when supported; in Bob, choose a service or plugin that supports the endpoint. Test a short passage, then inspect long-page segmentation, speed and limits, and screenshot text recognition. Keep keys in a password manager or the application's credential storage, with placeholders and explanations in shared configuration.

For example, Bitwarden CLI can manage passwords, API keys, and access tokens: retain credentials in the vault and let tools retrieve the relevant item through the command line when needed. Ask the model to configure and verify this retrieval path. Public files keep item references, placeholders, and usage notes; actual secret values stay out of chat, logs, and Git. Access to vault data needs a valid authenticated and unlocked session, arranged for the actual environment.

The person's reading language and the model's working language can differ. This guide uses the following arrangement: human-facing material uses the person's native language; technical notes, handoffs, and tool instructions primarily maintained by models default to English. English documentation, terminology, and interfaces make that arrangement convenient. Whether it improves a particular model's performance on a particular task depends on actual results; it does not establish that every model always works better in English. Preserve the required language and format of sources, quotations, code, paths, and interface fields. An English implementation note should not push translation work back onto the person who needs the result.

You can tell the model: “Discuss the work with me in my native language, including the results, evidence, and choices I need to judge. Use English by default for technical material that another model will maintain. Preserve originals, code, and identifiers accurately, and explain any English passage I need to understand where it appears.” Translation services may send selected text or screenshots to the configured provider; choose handling for private material according to its actual destination.

Broaden information sources while retaining judgment

In this working route, Telegram primarily helps locate subscription purchase channels and other services, goods, and miscellaneous resources, as well as contact sellers, compare offers, and handle follow-up. Channels and groups provide information and contact; the particular provider owns the transaction. Distinguish official subscriptions, third-party purchasing services, and shared plans, checking what is delivered, its duration, renewal, and account ownership. Evaluate channels by continued usability and support before price; do not sacrifice the primary subscription's reliability for a discount or treat group size and seller claims as proof of reliability. Telegram can also supplement everyday information, but it is not presented here as the main tool for collecting papers or specialist sources.

Find best practices and check documentation freshness

To understand how a tool actually behaves now, prioritize recent community Issues, PRs, and use reports that identify versions and provide reproducible steps. Check the date, client version, platform, and relevant account conditions, then whether a problem has been fixed or a recommendation still applies. Official documentation can also lag; use current official entrypoints for specific interfaces, configuration, APIs, and service availability. When accounts conflict, let the model compare their applicable conditions and check with an operation in the actual environment, rather than deciding by the source's name alone.

What you need to understand Basic entrypoints
Community practice and current problems Claude Code Best Practice covers agents, commands, Skills, Hooks, MCP, plugins, settings, and workflows; use Codex Issues and Claude Code Issues for concrete reports and follow-up.
Using ChatGPT and Codex ChatGPT / Codex documentation and the OpenAI Help Center.
GPT and API development OpenAI API documentation for interfaces and development configuration.
Using and developing with Claude The Claude Help Center, Claude Code documentation, and Claude API documentation.

A best-practice repository supplies methods to compare and adapt. Let the model read the parts relevant to the current task, check dependencies, versions, and actual effects, then choose what to adopt or change. Installing the whole collection or blindly copying its commands is unnecessary. Community reports can also be outdated or conditional; retain evidence you can revisit.

Resource access and conditional judgments about unauthorized copies

The legitimacy of a resource needs more than a paid-versus-free distinction. Author-posted manuscripts, open-access papers, public-domain works, openly licensed material, and library resources have their own access and use conditions. Free does not mean pirated. Ask the model to locate a suitable version and check its content, source, and intended use, rather than finding only a downloadable link. WIPO's copyright FAQ introduces the distinctions between permission, the public domain, and exceptions.

Anna's Archive and Sci-Hub can also enter your assessment of resource channels. The former aggregates records for books and papers, while the latter focuses on scholarly articles. These sites involve unauthorized copies and copyright disputes, so assess particular material under the conditions below. Domains and accessibility change; consult the background and entry information for Anna's Archive and Sci-Hub, and verify the current source rather than treating every similarly named mirror as the same site.

For material suspected of circulating without authorization, availability, financial circumstances, private study, and effects on creators can enter an ethical discussion. Those considerations do not automatically establish permission to copy, distribute, or use it. Reading, retaining a copy, redistribution, and commercial use are different acts; assess the particular resource's permissions and applicable rules, preserve attribution, and do not treat possession of a copy as a right to distribute it further. Software also raises questions about executable origin and integrity: prefer trustworthy open-source alternatives, trials, or educational access, and do not treat an unverified cracked installer as ordinary reading material.
